model.name: RecursiveRegressionForecaster

schema.description: Schema that configures the recursive regression forecaster.

regressor.description: The regression model that predicts the next value from the previous ones, along with its own configuration. A linear regression extends a trend; trees and forests cannot forecast past the values they were trained on.
regressor.title: Regressor

lags.description: How many past values the regressor reads to predict the next one. Left empty, it reads one season: Season length, or the season of the series' frequency when that is empty too (monthly: 12, daily: 7, hourly: 24), and at least 3. A number sets another count.
lags.title: Lags

season_length.description: How many steps make up one season. Only used for the default lags: it sets how many lags are read when Lags is left empty; it does not model the seasonality. Left empty, it uses the season of the series' frequency (monthly: 12, daily: 7, hourly: 24; 1 when it implies none). A number sets another cycle.
season_length.title: Season length

differentiation.description: How many times to difference the series before regressing on it. Use 1 on a series with a trend: the regressor then predicts the changes, which a tree can do where it cannot predict values it has never seen. 0 leaves the series as it is.
differentiation.title: Differencing

use_exogenous.description: Read the session's exogenous variables. Turn it off to compare the same model without them.
use_exogenous.title: Use exogenous variables

schema.title: RecursiveRegressionForecasterSchema

model.description: Turns forecasting into regression: a regression model learns each value from the previous ones and forecasts one step at a time. The intervals bootstrap the training errors, so with trees they come out too narrow; the backtest coverage shows it. With exogenous variables, the backtest error and coverage are optimistic.

schema.description:
Schema that configures the Ordinary Least-Squares Linear Regression model.

Linear Regression fits a linear model by minimising the residual sum of squares
between observed targets and predicted values. It is used for tabular regression
tasks. The underlying implementation is
``sklearn.linear_model.LinearRegression``.

fit_intercept.description: Whether to calculate the intercept for this model. If set to False, no intercept will be used in calculations (e.g., data is expected to be centered).
fit_intercept.title: Fit intercept

copy_X.description: If True, X will be copied; else, it may be overwritten.
copy_X.title: Copy X

n_jobs.description: The number of jobs to use for the computation. None means 1 job, while -1 means using all processors.
n_jobs.title: N jobs

positive.description: When set to True, forces the coefficients to be positive.
positive.title: Positive

schema.title: LinearRegressionSchema
